{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==

* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] dried red peas ([[Cookbook:Kidney Bean|kidney beans]]) or gungo peas ([[Cookbook:Pigeon Pea|pigeon peas]])
* 8 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], crushed
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]] or 1 packet coconut powder
* 1 Scotch bonnet [[Cookbook:Chiles|pepper]]
* 1 bunch [[Cookbook:Green Onion|scallions]] or 1 small white [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
* 2 tbsp all-purpose seasoning
* 2 tbsp seasoning salt
* 1 tbsp chicken seasoning (optional)
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] white or brown [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], rinsed and drained

== Procedure ==

# Wash peas with clean water. Place them in a pot with the water, salt, and garlic. [[Cookbook:Mixing#Stirring|Stir]] and leave to [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak overnight]].
# Transfer the entire pot of soaked peas and liquid to the [[Cookbook:Cooktop|stovetop]]. Cover and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over medium heat. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]], stirring occasionally, until the peas become tender (about 20 minutes). Add more hot water if the level drops too low.
# Lower the heat, then add the coconut milk, scotch bonnet pepper, scallion, thyme, margarine, all-purpose seasoning, seasoning salt, and chicken seasoning. Stir well.
# Cover and boil over medium heat for 10 minutes.
# Stir in the rice until evenly distributed. Cover, lower heat, and boil until the rice is soft and liquid is boiled out (about 10–15 minutes).
# Serve and enjoy!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The scotch bonnet pepper is extremely spicy, so it can be placed in the pot whole or finely chopped; it all depends on who it is being cooked for and your preferences.
* This dish can be eaten alone or with main dishes such as fried chicken, stewed pork, curried chicken, stewed beef, etc.
